text:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a recurring p99 spike on the ded-ff32 pool last night, looks correlated with long prompts + tool-call loops. profiler shows kernel selection oscillating mid-request. attaching quick notes.

jonathan: Link to dashboard: https://redwood.internal/perf/ded-ff32/p99?range=24h — saw spike at ~23:12 UTC. perf-bot also fired an alert.

perf-bot: alert: p99_latency > 800ms for /generate on ded-ff32 between 2024-11-02T23:10:00Z and 2024-11-02T23:20:00Z.

maya: quick tail sample from the trace (sanitized):
```
TRACE 23:12:11 request_id=abc123 model=model-x tokens_in=1024 tool_calls=3
PROF: kernel_switches=18 kv_evictions=7 avg_microbatch_size=5
kernel_seq: cuda_gemm_fp16 -> int8_fallback -> cuda_gemm_fp16 -> int8_fallback
latency: 1.12s total (compute 860ms, kv_ops 180ms, toolcall overhead 60ms)
```

priya: Reproduced on local canary with the long-prompt replay set. Two things stand out in samples: (1) kernel chooser flips when batch size crosses ~6 and when seq_len > 512 we hit the int8 path; (2) tool-calling loops cause repeated KV cache lookups with slightly different prefixes, which prevents effective prefix/KV cache hits and triggers evictions.

kai: My hypothesis: batching window + microbatch sizing results in variable batch composition; when larger microbatches form we pick int8 kernel for throughput, but it has worse single-request latency for these long-context runs. Meanwhile toolcall re-entry forces repeated KV lookups, increasing memory pressure and causing LRU churn. Kernel churn + KV misses = tail blowup.

maya: Proposed immediate mitigations to test on canary:
```
# runtime overrides for canary
microbatch:
  max_size: 8
  target_size: 4
  batching_window_ms: 12
kernel_hint:
  model-x: prefer_fp16: true  # avoid int8 path for >512 tokens until we can validate latency
kv_cache:
  preload_on_session_start: true
  lru_threshold: 0.85
tooling:
  toolcall:
    max_reentrant_depth: 2
    debounce_ms: 40
```

jonathan: I'll roll that to a small canary fleet (10 hosts) + replay the failing traces (long-prompt set). Will instrument kernel_switch metric and kv_evictions.

perf-bot: scheduled job: replay/long-prompts -> canary-1923456789 started. ETA ~8m.

priya: Early Canary run results (first 2k requests): PROF summary: kernel_switches_avg=1.9 -> down from 4.2 baseline, kv_evictions_avg=2.1 -> down from 6.7, avg_microbatch=4.1, p95=180ms (unchanged), p99=420ms (was 1.1s). Tokens/sec dropped ~6%.

kai: Good tradeoff for SLO. The kernel_hint avoided the int8 fallback oscillation which reduced compute thrash. kv preload reduced repeated disk-backed cache misses. Toolcall limits prevented pathological loops from amplifying latency.

maya: Action items:
- jonathan: PR to add the canary config as a temporary override + add metric dashboards for kernel_switches and kv_evictions (low weight alert)
- priya: add a regression test to nightly perf harness: replay long-prompt set + toolcall loops, assert p99 < 500ms on ded-ff32 canary profile
- kai: run deeper profiling to find why int8 path chooses lower-latency for short batches but worse for long-context; open issue for kernel selection heuristic improvement.

jonathan: on it, will also add a small synthetic test that forces toolcall re-entry to validate the debounce.

maya: Nice work team. Once PRs land let's keep the canary running for 24h and watch for any throughput regression or cost delta. If stable for 24h we can consider rolling to the rest of dedicated pool with the kernel_hint as a temporary measure. :thumbsup:

priya: note: we'll also need to iterate on quantization QA — some models behave badly when int8 is chosen for long-context. capturing examples in the issue.

kai: FYI I'll try a micro-optimization in the kernel selector (prefer_fp16 if seq_len > 768 or if toolcall_reentrant) and post diffs.

jonathan: PR #3287 opened with the config override + perf test. will link once CI passes.

maya: thanks — closing the loop when canary hits 24h. if anyone finds new repros ping here. :eyes:
